page: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the Eadv6 server family. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, featuring 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided by a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is a notable tradeoff, with read-only bandwidth for both small and large blocks scoring in the bottom 25%, though write bandwidth remains average. Text processing performance is strong, while database operations, software compilation, and Redis SET operations are weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ads_v6 offers a high memory density relative to its vCPU count, making it suitable for workloads that require substantial RAM without demanding high-density parallel compute. The presence of a local NVMe SSD provides fast local scratch space. This server is best suited for memory-intensive workloads such as medium-sized databases, caching layers, memory-bound web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications that benefit from a high memory-to-vCPU ratio.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ads_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 2 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities and text processing, though multi-core performance and memory read bandwidth are average to weak. Database operations and Redis SET throughput also rank in the lower tier. The instance utilizes Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES cryptography. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that do not require massive parallel compute, making it well-suited for memory-bound applications, caching layers, and database workloads.
